svg.title: IdTable::erase(A): backward-shift deletion
svg.text: open addressing with linear probing, 8 slots; each key shows its home slot = mix(id) & mask

g.text: Linear probing. A and B both hash to slot 2: B sits one further. C (home 3) was pushed to 4.
find(B): start at home 2 → not B → slot 3 → found.
find(C): start at home 3 (holds B) → slot 4 → found. A lookup stops at the first EMPTY slot.
The wrong way to erase A: just empty slot 2. Now find(B) starts at 2, sees empty, and stops.
B is still in the table but can no longer be found ✗
Backward shift. Hole i = 2. Look at j = 3 (B): distance from home 3 − 2 = 1 ≥ distance to hole 1 → move.
B is now at its home. Hole i = 3. j = 4 (C, home 3): 4 − 3 = 1 ≥ 4 − 3 = 1 → move.
Hole i = 4. j = 5 (D, home 5): distance from home 0 ≥ 1? No. D stays: moving it would put it before its home.
j = 6 is empty: the run ends. Slot 4 is set to empty. No tombstone is left behind.
find(B): slot 2 ✓ find(C): slot 3 ✓ find(D): slot 5 ✓ find(A): slot 2, 3, 4 → empty → not found ✓
